issue.title: SSLPeerUnverifiedException: peer not verified when using OpenSSL provider

repository.name: netty-tcnative
repository.description: A fork of Apache Tomcat Native, based on finagle-native

issue.body: Don't know if this is netty or netty-tcnative related: https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/4722

body:
Interesting... Can you give us a reproducer?

> Am 17.01.2016 um 18:44 schrieb floragunn UG notifications@github.com:
> 
> When using netty with JDK SSL Provider all works well, if i use Open SSL Provider i always get a
> 
> javaxnetsslSSLPeerUnverifiedException: peer not verified at ionettyhandlersslOpenSslEngine$OpenSslSessiongetPeerCertificateChain(OpenSslEnginejava:1644)
> 
> although the client sends a valid client certificate with cert chain included (cause with JDK SSL Provider its working fine) Open SSL works perfect for one way SSL but as soon the client needs to authenticate to the server the above mentioned exception occurs
> Netty 4033 with netty-tcnative 1133Fork10 on osx-x86_64 an OpenSSL 102d 9 Jul 2015
> 
> —
> Reply to this email directly or view it on GitHub.

@floragunncom I tried to reproduce with 4.0 branch but no luck. Please provide a reproducer or preferable a testcase. Maybe you can adjust https://github.com/netty/netty/blob/4.0/handler/src/test/java/io/netty/handler/ssl/SSLEngineTest.java to show the problem ?

reproduce with that: https://github.com/floragunncom/netty/commit/fe2d3acc8faa59044132b89f8278c34f5aa12543

If you set SSLProvider in Main.java to JDK then it works

repository.name: netty
repository.description: Netty project - an event-driven asynchronous network application framework

issue.body:

With JDK provider it fails correctly:

issue.body:
Netty version : 4.1 - ff11fe8 also tried with netty-4.1.0.Beta8
When trying to connect to a host with SNI enabled from the netty openssl client, handshake fails as :

```
OpenSSL error: error:14077410:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:sslv3 alert handshake failure
```

same issue when you use the openssl s_client :

```
openssl s_client -connect sni-enabled-host:443
140133327337120:error:14077410:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:sslv3 alert handshake failure:s23_clnt.c:770:
```

and works well for : 

```
openssl s_client -connect sni-enabled-host:443 -servername sni-enabled-host
```

The following code fails with Openssl and gives the same error but works fine with Openssl disabled (removed netty-tcnative) 

```
SSLEngine sslEngine = sslCtx.newEngine(ctx.channel().alloc(), peerHost,peerPort));
```
